findings.claim: this is what lifts you from Level 1 to Level 3
findings.truth: Band names of the form 'Level N' are banned house-wide; use Low band / Mid band / Top band.
findings.evidence: house rule in CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned-string list

findings.claim: Card 4: answer 'RealWorld', question '_____ Examples of Inorganic Growth Merger - T-Mobile and Orange (2009): ... to create a company with 28'
findings.truth: The card is an auto-generated cloze cut out of a collapsible heading and truncated mid-number. Replaced with a public limited company term card.

findings.claim: Merger - Disney and Pixar (2006): Disney bought Pixar for $7.4 billion.
findings.truth: Disney acquired Pixar in an all-stock deal announced January 2006 and completed May 2006. It was a friendly takeover, not a merger, and the sentence itself says Disney bought Pixar.

findings.claim: Kraft bought Cadbury for GBP 11.7 billion
findings.truth: The offer Cadbury accepted on 19 January 2010 valued the company at GBP 11.5 billion. The Somerdale closure cost 400 jobs, so 'hundreds' is sound.

findings.claim: There are currently around 1,400 companies on the London Stock Exchange
findings.truth: Main Market plus AIM has run at roughly 1,600-1,900 companies over the last few years. The figure is stale but hedged with 'around', and it drifts every year, so it is not worth an edit now.
findings.evidence: no single current source fetched; flagged for the next data refresh

findings.claim: Merger - T-Mobile and Orange (2009)
findings.truth: The joint venture was announced in September 2009 and completed on 1 April 2010 as Everything Everywhere. The 28.4 million customer figure is right.

findings.claim: Edexcel identifies five key reasons ... / The Edexcel specification also requires you to know how aims and objectives change
findings.truth: Student-facing text must never name the exam board. Both sentences rewritten without it.

findings.claim: Card 4: answer 'Julyrdquo', question 'increase online sales by 8% by _____'
findings.truth: A mangled HTML entity (July”) became the answer. Replaced with a product range term card.

findings.claim: they had previously stocked 228 types of air freshener
findings.truth: The figure reported when Tesco announced the 30% range cut in January 2015 is usually given as 224 air fresheners and 28 tomato ketchups. I could not reach a source to confirm, so no edit. The 90,000 lines and 30% cut are sound.
findings.evidence: Guardian, BBC and Independent pages all blocked for this session

findings.claim: with over 230 million subscribers
findings.truth: Netflix reported 301.6 million paid memberships at the end of 2024 and stopped reporting the figure in 2025. 'Over 230 million' is literally true but badly out of date.

findings.claim: Coca-Cola, for example, operates in 188 countries worldwide.
findings.truth: The Coca-Cola Company sells its drinks in more than 200 countries and territories.

findings.claim: businesses likely to pollute the air must gain a permit to trade, or face up to six months in prison and a GBP 20,000 fine
findings.truth: Under the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 reg.39 the penalty is up to 12 months' imprisonment on summary conviction and up to 5 years on indictment, with an unlimited fine in both cases. There is no GBP 20,000 cap.

findings.claim: Card 4: answer 'Avoiding', question '_____ child labour - about 14 million children worldwide ...'
findings.truth: An auto-generated cloze with the blank at the start and a gerund as the answer. Replaced with a pressure groups term card.

findings.claim: Q3 'Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for a business of trading ethically' labelled 3 marks - Explain
findings.truth: An Explain question asks for one statement plus two expansion points. This one asks for two sides and its mark scheme lists four credit points capped at 3. It is self-consistent enough to leave, but it models the wrong shape.

findings.claim: A Bugatti Veyron, the fastest car in the world at 301 mph, prioritises function above all else.
findings.truth: The Veyron Super Sport set the production-car record at 431.072 km/h (267.856 mph) on 4 July 2010. The Veyron was never recorded at 301 mph; that figure belongs to the Chiron Super Sport 300+, and the Veyron is no longer the fastest car in the world.

findings.claim: The VW Golf has been modified through nine generations since 1974
findings.truth: There have been eight generations: Mk1 (1974), Mk2 (1983), Mk3 (1991), Mk4 (1997), Mk5 (2003), Mk6 (2008), Mk7 (2012), Mk8 (2019).

findings.claim: Cards 4 and 5 are cloze questions that open with the blank: '_____ refers to how well a product works ...'
findings.truth: Single-word answers need a question that starts What / Which / Who / When / Name. Both rewritten as 'Which element of the design mix ...' questions; the answers Function and Aesthetics are kept.

findings.claim: BlackBerry smartphones were withdrawn in 2016
findings.truth: BlackBerry stopped designing its own handsets in September 2016. BlackBerry-branded phones carried on under licence (TCL) until 2020, and legacy services closed in January 2022. Loose rather than wrong.

findings.claim: The Edexcel specification requires you to know five key strategies ... / five key pricing strategies for Edexcel Business
findings.truth: Two problems in one sentence pair: the board is named in student-facing text, and topic 2.2.2 lists only 'pricing strategies' plus the influences on them, so the spec does not itself set these five. Rewritten as 'five key strategies to learn'.

findings.claim: Product life cycle defined as 'introduction, growth, maturity, and decline' in lessons 6 and 9
findings.truth: Lesson 5 teaches five stages, opening with research and development, and its key fact, knowledge check and flashcards all use five. Lessons 6 and 9 contradict it. Both definitions aligned to the five-stage version.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with lesson 5; spec topic 2.2.1 says only 'the phases of the product life cycle'

findings.claim: The Edexcel specification requires you to understand five main promotion strategies / The five core promotion strategies on the Edexcel spec are / revision tip 'from the Edexcel spec'
findings.truth: Three separate places name the board in student-facing text, including a revision tip.

findings.claim: Top band mark scheme reads 'E.g. builds on Level 2 plus:'
findings.truth: 'Level 2' is a banned band name. Replaced with 'builds on the mid band plus'.
findings.evidence: house rule in CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned-string list

findings.claim: Q5 text 'Analyse the impact on KFC of using special offers' carries the label '6 marks - Discuss'
findings.truth: The taxonomy separates the two: Analyse is placed in context by the question, Discuss is not. The question gives context (KFC), so the command word is right and the label is wrong.

findings.claim: Q6 mark scheme: 'the target market is local car/computer owners'
findings.truth: The question is about a computer repair business. 'car/' is a copy-paste artefact from another context and confuses the answer key.
findings.evidence: internal check against the question stem

findings.claim: The Old Spice campaign 'gained over 60 million views and boosted body wash sales by 60%'
findings.truth: Reported figures for the 2010 campaign vary widely (55% over three months, 107% in the month after the response films). I could not confirm either number, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Old Spice, carries no figures

findings.claim: The Edexcel specification requires you to understand two main methods of distribution
findings.truth: Student-facing text must never name the exam board.

findings.claim: Card 4: answer 'Marketing', question 'The _____ Mix - A Quick Recap The marketing mix refers to ...'
findings.truth: An auto-generated cloze cut out of a heading, and the answer word appears again in its own question. Replaced with a 'Which of the 4Ps' card answered 'Place'.

findings.claim: Iceland ... 'Sales revenue and profits increased by GBP 9.5 million.'
findings.truth: One figure is given for two different measures, with no year and no source, so a student cannot use it and cannot check it. Two options: (a) delete the sentence, which loses nothing because the rest of the case study carries the point, or (b) replace it with a sourced Iceland Foods figure from a published annual report. I recommend (a) unless Tom wants the numbers kept, in which case the figure needs a year and a source.
findings.evidence: no source found for the figure

findings.claim: 9-mark mark scheme bands 'Lower band (1-2) / Mid band (3-5) / Top band (6-9)'
findings.truth: The bands are uneven and do not match the rest of the unit, which uses 1-3 / 4-6 / 7-9 for a 9-mark question.

findings.claim: The Edexcel specification identifies five key factors that affect supplier relationships
findings.truth: Student-facing text must never name the exam board.

findings.claim: KC2: 'according to the Edexcel spec'
findings.truth: A knowledge check a student reads names the board. Removed; the answer key (Advertising, index 3) is correct and unchanged.

findings.claim: 9-mark mark scheme bands 'Lower band (1-2) / Mid band (3-5) / Top band (6-9)'
findings.truth: Same uneven bands as lesson 10.

findings.claim: 'Edexcel wants you to know two methods of managing quality', 'Edexcel wants you to know five key factors of the sales process', and a revision tip naming Edexcel
findings.truth: Three places name the board in student-facing text.

findings.claim: KC2: 'a factor of the sales process that Edexcel requires you to know'
findings.truth: Names the board in a knowledge check. Answer key unchanged.

findings.claim: Card 4: answer 'Quality', question 'QA methods include Total _____ Management (TQM) ...'
findings.truth: The answer duplicates card 1's answer 'quality' within the same deck, and the cloze does not open with a question word. Replaced with a post-sales service card.
findings.evidence: house flashcard rules (unique answers, cloze question openers)

findings.claim: 12-mark mark scheme awards application marks for 'The new chef from Switzerland has introduced new products' and 'as the business expands to new premises'
findings.truth: The question stem gives none of this: it says only that the business is a small private limited company in Devon making hand-made desserts and that a new chef plans a QA system. A student cannot apply information they were never given.
findings.evidence: internal check against the question stem

findings.claim: Ocado 'built a 62% excellent Trustpilot rating'
findings.truth: A live review score that moves every week and cannot be pinned to a date. Not worth an edit, but it should go if the lesson is ever rebuilt.

findings.claim: 'In the Edexcel GCSE Business exam', 'formulas in the Edexcel exam', and a revision tip asking 'will Edexcel provide formulas?'
findings.truth: Three places name the board. The underlying claim is correct: the spec says formulae will not be provided in the examinations for Paper 1 or Paper 2.

findings.claim: Q3 'Calculate the gross profit and the gross profit margin' labelled '3 marks - Explain'
findings.truth: Calculate is its own command word in the taxonomy. The label is wrong, not the question.

findings.claim: Net Profit = Gross Profit - Operating Costs
findings.truth: The spec formula is 'net profit = gross profit - other operating expenses and interest'. The lesson's worked examples do label the deduction 'Operating Expenses & Interest' and the NPM example uses 'operating costs & interest', so the teaching is right even though the headline formula drops the word interest.

findings.claim: Q5 mark scheme lists 'relying on road upgrades' among the drawbacks of relocating
findings.truth: The stem for Shultz & Sheiff says nothing about roads. A leftover from another context, but harmless because it sits inside a bracketed list of examples.
findings.evidence: internal check against the question stem

findings.claim: 'Three key theorists are studied at GCSE level' and 'In the exam, you need to be able to compare these theories and apply them to business scenarios'
findings.truth: Topic 2.5.4 Motivation names no theorist. It sets financial methods (remuneration, bonus, commission, promotion, fringe benefits) and non-financial methods (job rotation, job enrichment, autonomy). Taylor, Maslow and Herzberg are useful background but must not be presented as examinable content, and none of the methods the spec does list appear in the lesson.

findings.claim: Q6 worded 'Evaluate whether ...' but labelled '9 marks - Justify'
findings.truth: Evaluate and Justify are different command words in the taxonomy, and the rest of the unit uses Justify at 9 marks and Evaluate at 12. The wording was changed to match the label.

summary: 15 lessons checked against the 1BS0 specification. Every calculation in lessons 13 and 14 recomputes correctly and every formula matches Appendix 3, and all 75 knowledge check answer keys are right. The real damage is elsewhere: two banned band names, five mangled auto-generated flashcards, seventeen places that name the exam board in student-facing text, a wrong Bugatti top speed, a wrong Golf generation count, a wrong Coca-Cola country count, a wrong Cadbury price, a mislabelled Disney-Pixar deal, a wrong environmental permit penalty, and Taylor, Maslow and Herzberg taught as examinable when topic 2.5.4 names no theorist.
